names.note: Latin name of the Roman colony. No Arabic form is given because the name was Latin; Arabic sources later render it Iliya (next entry). Masalha dates the renaming only to the 2nd century, so the start is the century's first year with circa set, as in the event record; a second source should place it in the 130s. He says the name stayed official until the Arab conquest, which he dates to 638 (the surrender is also given as 637); the end is set to the year before Iliya begins so the two names do not overlap.

names.note: The name of the country in Roman and Byzantine sources, as Masalha cites them: the official form Syria Palaestina from a 139 military diploma, Ptolemy about 150, Eusebius in the early 4th century, the three Palestines at Chalcedon in 451 and Palaestina Prima by 484. No Arabic form is given because the name was Latin and Greek. The end is the Arab conquest (636-638), after which Byzantine control was lost for good (Masalha, p. 98-99). The provincial subdivisions (Prima, Secunda, Tertia, Salutaris) are not separated here for lack of dated sources.
